title: Senior Manager, Privacy and Access to Information
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
The Royal Canadian Mint (the Mint) is hiring a Senior Manager, Privacy and Access to Information who can thrive in a dynamic and inclusive environment.
Reporting to the Senior Director, Regulatory and Corporate Affairs, the Senior Manager, Privacy and Access to Information is responsible for ensuring the Mint’s management of the Privacy, Access to Information, CASL and Parliamentary questions programs include key program design and statutory and regulatory as applicable. The Senior Manager will lead and assign work under this portfolio to the ATIP team.
Your Responsibilities:
- Promote and support the mandate of the ATIP office and the Mint’s Privacy Program which includes protecting the Mint’s directors, officers and employees from the serious adverse consequences of non-compliance with privacy legislation (including regulatory sanction and damage to reputation), CASL and Access to Information legislation.
- Responsible for the day-to-day management of access to information, CASL, Parliamentary Questions and privacy-related programs throughout the Mint to foster a culture of privacy by leading and supporting the integration of privacy considerations in organizational activities and decisions, developing of tools and resources, and delivering employee training awareness/building awareness.
- Develop the Mint’s privacy policy governance framework to support the Mint’s mission and to ensure that corporate privacy policies and practices align with legislative requirements and best practices.
- Manage two ATIP team members to ensure the accuracy and timeliness of Access and Privacy Act access responses and maintenance of accurate records and compliance with all reporting requirements under the applicable legislation.
- Provide technical and professional advisory and compliance services on all aspects of privacy and privacy-related queries for the organization, including Privacy Impact Assessments, procurement processes, and the oversight of consultants as needed.
- Develop annual work plans to prioritize and implement privacy deliverables aligned with internal stakeholders’ and organizational programs and/or initiatives.
- Act as the privacy representative on senior committees as required to promote best practices and excellent customer service on privacy-related matters including on the AI Council
- Responsible for liaison with external stakeholders, the Treasury Board Secretariat and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner, including for the resolution of complaints.
- Manage the ATIP Office’s responsibilities and actions for the privacy incident/breach response process (investigation, assessment, reporting, mitigation/prevention oversight, etc.)
- Support the ATIP Office’s operational work as required by providing high-level expertise on ATIP request files.
This position offers a hybrid work arrangement, requiring on-site presence at our Ottawa location three to five days per week, depending on meeting requirements and other activities.
This selection process may also qualify you for other positions with similar requirements and qualifications.
Qualifications:
Languages Requirements:
Proficiency in both official languages (English & French) is required at the time of hire. The linguistic profile for this position is:
- Reading Comprehension : C Advanced
- Written Expression : B Intermediate
- Oral Proficiency : C Advanced
If no qualified candidate fully meets the linguistic profile of the position, other bilingual profiles may be considered, in accordance with the Mint’s Staffing Policy.
Education & Designation:
- University Degree in related field
- Professional privacy certification (CIPP/C) or commensurate designation.
Experience:
- Minimum of 10 years of related business experience
- Minimum of 7 years of progressive management experience.
Additional Qualifications:
- Advanced knowledge of Canadian and international privacy legislation, familiarity with the Access to Information Act, and excellent knowledge of TBS policies, directives and privacy best practices as they apply to Crown corporations.
- Ability to interpret laws, regulations and legal advice.
- Able to solicit and keep the goodwill and cooperation of a wide range of individuals, including operational staff and senior management, while providing advice, guidance and strategic influencing on complex privacy compliance issues.
- Proficient at written and verbal communications, in particular, the development of succinct and useful reporting on compliance issues for a senior management audience.
- Sound judgment and a strong practical approach to considering courses of action.
- The flexibility to balance multiple accountabilities with competing priorities; and
- The ability to work independently and to meet tight deadlines, and to quickly adapt to unforeseen circumstances, changes in priorities and initiatives.
Why the Mint?
At the Mint, you will collaborate with a diverse group of people and be a part of an iconic Canadian organization. Your safety and wellbeing are our top priority. We offer outstanding pay and total rewards for you and your family and you will be supported to continuously learn throughout your career.
The Mint is committed to building an inclusive workforce that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, and skills. We value diversity and aim to provide an inclusive, barrier-free recruitment, selection and onboarding process to ensure that each candidate is treated respectfully.
If you need accommodation at any point in the application or interview process, please let us know. We are committed to being an inclusive employer. For a confidential inquiry, simply email us directly at ee@mint.ca to make arrangements.
What to Expect
In order to be considered for an interview, please clearly demonstrate on your application how you meet the education and experience qualifications. The additional qualifications may be assessed through interviews, exams, reference checks, etc. If successful, you will be required to complete a background check facilitated by the Mint in order to obtain a security clearance.
Ready to mint your career?
Please forward your resume to careers@mint.ca by October 22, 2026. We look forward to receiving your application!

title: Developer/Senior Developer - Payments and Tokenization
description:
Language requirements: English or French essential
Developer/Senior Developer - Payments and Tokenization
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
Shape the Future of Payments and Financial Technology. We are seeking a motivated Developer to help design and deliver secure solutions across payments, tokenization, blockchain, digital assets, and distributed ledger technologies (DLT). Working closely with the Bank for International Settlements Innovation Hub (BISIH) in Toronto, you will contribute to innovate projects that address complex challenges in the evolving financial technology landscape. We are looking for a collaborative and curious individual with a passion for emerging technologies and a commitment to continuous learning and innovation.
What you will be working on You will work collaboratively with our team to help design and deliver scalable, secure and practical technology solutions in payments, tokenisation, digital assets and distributed ledger systems:
- Develop technology solutions and prototypes that explore and advance use cases in payments, tokenisation, digital assets, and distributed ledger systems.
- Contribute to the technical design and implementation of systems involving payment flows, settlement processes, tokenised assets, ledger integrations, smart contract-enabled workflows, wallet interactions and related digital finance infrastructure.
- Build and maintain high-quality backend services, APIs, integration layers, developer tools, and other core platform components.
- Evaluate technical approaches and provide input on architecture, tooling implementation patterns, and the appropriate use of DLTs.
- Collaborate with technical leads and stakeholders to define requirements, solutions options, implementation plans, and acceptance criteria.
- Identify technical risks, performance concerns, and design challenges, and propose practical solutions.
- Prepare clear technical documentation and communicate complex concepts to both technical and non-technical audiences.
- Contribute to engineering best practices, including code quality, testing, security, observability, maintainability, and release management.
- Stay current on emerging technologies, standards, and industry developments, and translate insights into practical recommendations and solutions. Participate in technical discussions, code reviews, and knowledge-sharing activities while contributing to a collaborative, delivery-focused team environment.
What you need to succeed We are looking for candidates who demonstrate the following skills and competencies. We welcome applicants who may not meet every requirement but have a strong foundation and a willingness to continue learning and growing.
- Familiarity with blockchain concepts, consensus algorithms, smart contracts and DeFi ecosystem including cross-chain and off-chain transfers, atomic swaps and oracle
- Experience or capability of developing tokenized solutions on DLT platforms using Solidity, Move or similar technologies.
- Strong programming skills in one or more modern languages such as Java, Kotlin, Go, C#, TypeScript, Python or Rust.
- Knowledge of one or more following areas: payments, transaction flows, settlement, tokenisation, stablecoins, digital assets, market infrastructure or regulated financial systems.
- Understanding of wallet and custody integrations, interoperability approaches, and key security, privacy, identity, access management, and resilience considerations in financial technology environments.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, sound judgment, and a pragmatic approach to innovation and delivery.
- Ability to work independently in an dynamic environment while collaborating effectively with multidisciplinary teams.
Nice-to-have
- Experience with token standards, token lifecycle design, smart contract review, or related controls supporting safe deployment of contract-based systems.
- Exposure to payment standards, market infrastructure standards or regulated financial technology environments.
- Experience or academic exposure to cloud-native development, containerization technologies, CI/CD pipelines and observability practices.
- Familiarity with cryptography, key management, digital identity or privacy-enhancing technologies or related security concepts
Your education and experience This position may be staffed at either the JG16 (Developer) or JG17 (Senior Developer) level, depending on the candidate's qualifications, experience, and demonstrated competencies.
Candidates must have a bachelor's degree in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field, along with: • 4 to 5 years of relevant experience for consideration at the JG16 (Developer) level; or • 5 to 7 years of relevant experience for consideration at the JG17 (Senior Developer) level.
An equivalent combination of education and practical project experience may also be considered. Recent graduates from a master's or PhD program in computer science, computer engineering, or a related field who have completed project work in blockchain, tokenization, smart contracts, or distributed ledger technologies (DLT) are encouraged to apply.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. Although the position language requirement is English or French essential, we do encourage everyone to improve their second language proficiency for future career growth and to contribute towards fostering a bilingual environment.
What you need to know
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Reliability Relocation assistance may be provided, if required Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available. The official title for this position is “Developer/Senior Developer ”
Hybrid Work Model
The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .
- Salaries are based on qualifications and experience and typically range from $94,193 to $110,816 (job grade 16) and from $111,051 to $130,649 (job grade 17) The Bank offers an incentive for successfully meeting expectations at between 5-10% (depending on job grade). Exceptional performers who far exceed expectations may be eligible for higher performance pay. Flexible and comprehensive benefits so you can choose the level of health and dental coverage that meets your needs Extra vacation days (up to five each year) that you can purchase to add to your vacation entitlement Option to join the indexed, defined-benefit pension plan after 24 consecutive months of service
We wish to thank all applicants for their interest and effort in applying for this position. Only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

About the position
Duties
Build your career where your work makes a visible difference. PacifiCan's northern offices offer a unique opportunity to contribute directly to the growth and prosperity of communities across northern British Columbia. Whether you are drawn to the natural beauty of the region, a strong sense of community, or the chance to work closely with local businesses and partners, you'll find rewarding career opportunities and meaningful work. Join a collaborative and supportive organization that values innovation, regional knowledge, and helping communities thrive.
____________________________________________________________________________
At PacifiCan, we support economic development through the following roles:
💼 Convenor – a trusted federal partner that understands local and regional circumstances and can make linkages within and outside of government to drive strategic investments and joint economic ventures.
💼 Pathfinder – connect entrepreneurs, economic development organizations and communities with federal programming and services to increase their participation in British Columbia's economy.
💼 Advisor – provide insights into regional economic issues to inform national policy and program decisions, and contribute to the development of regional engagement strategies and advice to the federal government.
💼 Investor – guide clients to access PacifiCan’s funding programs to capitalize on strategic regional investment opportunities or identify other sources of funding to support economic growth, job creation, improved economic competitiveness and other related objectives.
Work environment
PacifiCan is an innovative workplace that makes a difference in British Columbia. We consistently rank as a top federal department to work in, and we are driven to be the best at what we do. We hire top talent and provide an employment experience that brings out the best in people. We are motivated by achieving great results for British Columbians and Canadians.
Why should you consider a career with PacifiCan? If you join our team, you will:
✔️ Work with engaged people who support each other and love the work they do;
✔️ Contribute to meaningful work that strengthens the economy and makes a real difference in the lives of British Columbians and Canadians;
✔️ Enjoy a culture of continuous learning and support for your professional development;
✔️ Gain exposure to diverse economic sectors and issues of importance to the future economy;
✔️ Enjoy flexible work arrangements;
✔️ Work with modern tools and technology; and
✔️ Work with an innovative leadership team who is passionate about hiring and developing talent, and achieving results.
Please note: the successful candidate will be required to report to one of the Northern PacifiCan office locations (Fort St. John, Prince George, or Prince Rupert) under our hybrid work model.
Intent of the process
This is an anticipatory recruitment process that may be used to fill indeterminate vacancies in addition to temporary positions in Northern PacifiCan office locations (Fort St. John, Prince George, or Prince Rupert). This process will not be used to staff PacifiCan positions in any other locations.
In addition, this recruitment process may be used to establish a pool of qualified candidates to staff similar positions of various tenures (including but not limited to term and indeterminate appointments, internal assignments, secondments, deployments, and acting appointments). The pool may also be used to staff positions with various security requirements, language requirements, and conditions of employment.

About the position
Duties
Strategic Communications Unit
The Alberta RCMP Strategic Communications Unit is a fast-paced, work environment where no two days look the same. The unit provides communications assistance to all levels of the Alberta RCMP including all units and detachments. The positions in the unit provide a wide range of services for both internal and external audiences including media relations, social media management, strategic advice, crisis communications, communications planning, web support, video productions, and graphic design.
⭐Digital Media Group
The Digital Media Group manages the Alberta RCMP’s digital presence and visual communications, including social media channels, internal and external websites, video production, graphic design and photography. Its in-house specialists create communications products and provide technical and visual support for divisional operations and initiatives.
⭐Strategy Group
The Strategy Group leads communications projects that advance operational priorities, strengthen community engagement, and enhance the profile of the Alberta RCMP. The group develops proactive and responsive communications plans, messaging and campaigns for internal and external audiences, along with web and print copy, media materials, executive speaking notes and communiqués.
⭐Media Relations Group
The Media Relations Group provides timely, accurate, open and transparent communications that inform the public, support operational priorities, and strengthen trust and confidence in the RCMP. The group coordinates proactive and reactive media relations for the Alberta RCMP around the clock, ensures divisional media releases meet established quality standards and operating procedures, and supports media relations personnel through appropriate training, resources and divisional training initiatives.
Intent of the process
This is an anticipatory staffing process designed to create a pool of qualified candidates. The pool of qualified candidates may be used to staff similar positions with various tenures (i.e. indeterminate, term, deployment, acting, assignment and secondment) within the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.
Should a Civilian Member (CM) be found qualified and selected for appointment, the appointment will not result in a change of status to the Public Service (PS) category for the CM. Information regarding the CM appointment will be sent to all applicable candidates who are within the area of selection and participated in the advertised process.

Volume Management strategies may be used.
Candidates invited to the assessment stage will be required to provide ORIGINAL proof of their education credentials, i.e., their degree or official transcript. Failure to do so may result in you not being considered further in the selection process.
Candidates will be asked to provide proof of Canadian citizenship or permanent residency.

The process requires a Security/Reliability Interview, a field investigation in matters of credit/finances, education, employment, references, etc.

description:

About the position
Duties
Looking for a career where your work has a visible impact? This could be your opportunity to bring your expertise to Canada's North. The Governance and Partnerships sector is looking for talented people to join our team in Yellowknife, Northwest Territories.
Working in the North offers a unique opportunity to build relationships, contribute to meaningful files, broaden your professional experience and experience a part of Canada that few people get to know through their work.
DUTIES | WHAT YOU WILL DO
✔️Inspection Planning and Management: lead, plan and coordinate the inspection program with support from inspection staff. Monitor project progress and compliance in the field or through meetings with developers. Provide technical advice where appropriate to assist developers in maintaining compliance with regulatory authorizations and legislative requirements.
✔️ Financial: assist in the establishment of annual Operational and Maintenance (O&M) budget for the inspection program.

Looking for meaningful work where you can make a real difference? Join the Non-Insured Health Benefits (NIHB) Program and help eligible First Nations and Inuit clients access essential health benefits, including medical transportation, mental health services, vision care, and medical supplies and equipment.
By joining our team, you will have an opportunity to provide direct support to health services and community based programming. This position requires flexibility in work scheduling, including mandatory shifts and, when operationally required, overtime that may be requested on short notice to support service delivery and meet client needs. About the position
Duties
The student research project aims to evaluate the performance of ECCC’s chemical transport model (GEM-MACH) under the wintertime urban conditions observed during SWAPIT. The evaluation will include model-to-observation comparisons for multiple pollutants including, but not limited to, common air pollutants (e.g., NO2, O3, and PM), CO, VOCs, speciated PM, and size-distributed EC/OC, metals, and PAHs. The evaluation seeks not only to quantify model performance, but also to link model shortcomings to gaps in modelled emissions and/or atmospheric processing and to support the setting and design of research priorities. Depending on results of the evaluation, model experiments to query emissions and/or process scenarios may be carried out, and activities to advance urban-scale modelling from 2.5km to 250 m resolution may be conducted.

description:

Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
The role
We are seeking an instrumentation scientist or engineer who will play a lead role in the development of new astronomical instrumentation based on fiber optic and photonic chip technologies. The Instrumentation Scientist would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect, and Creativity. The successful candidate will participate in the TESERACT project, a CubeSat mission that will demonstrate a novel type of spectroscopy in space. As a Research Associate in our team, you will contribute to the instrumentation effort based on our photonic integral field unit (IFU) architecture through fiber-coupling, alignment, integration, on-sky and in-lab characterization. The long-term objective is a multi-object spectral characterization instrument for biosignature detection on Earth-like exoplanets, with applications in Earth observation. The work shifts from bulk optics to chip-scale photonic processing, improving size, weight, power, cost, stability, and scalability while maintaining high resolution. Key technical areas include:
- Integral field unit (IFU) and integral field spectroscopy feed design and integration
- Fiber-coupling, microlens arrays, and beam-remapping optics
- Optical design, alignment, and integration of instrument front-ends
- Photonic device and sub-system characterization at visible and near-infrared wavelengths
- On-sky commissioning and validation on ground-based telescopes
You will collaborate with researchers from NRC’s Quantum and Nanotechnologies Research Center, the University of Toronto, and Queen's University Belfast, with travel to collaborator sites.

- astronomical instrumentation hardware development.

- design or characterization of photonic chip technologies.

- Experience working in an astronomical instrumentation development team.
- Experience using or developing optical spectrographs, integral field units (IFUs) or adaptive optic systems.
- Experience with CubeSat or small satellite payloads and space systems engineering.

About the Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre
We are Canada's gateway to the stars. At the Herzberg Astronomy and Astrophysics Research Centre, we maintain and operate Canada's largest and most powerful observatories and represent the country in some of the world's leading astronomy initiatives. We are astronomy and astrophysics experts, conducting cutting-edge research, operating Canada's national observatories, providing extensive data management and analysis tools through our Canadian Astronomy Data Centre, supporting activities at international observatories and developing advanced astronomical instruments with industrial partners. More…
About DAO
The Dominion Astrophysical Observatory (DAO) offers capabilities in optical imaging, spectroscopy and spectropolarimetry, and currently operates two research telescopes: the 1.8-metre Plaskett Telescope and the 1.2-metre telescope, which features the high resolution McKellar spectrograph. The DAO conducts technology research and development associated with instrumentation, facility design and construction projects of the domestic, international and future telescopes they support. The Observatory has been designated a national historic site because of its important role in establishing Canada's international scientific reputation in astronomy. Over the decades, these telescopes have contributed significantly to our understanding of the rotation, size and mass of the Milky Way, and of the rarefied interstellar medium between the stars. Recent projects include orbital determination of comets and asteroids, spectroscopy of magnetic stars, and ongoing studies of distant quasars and galaxies. More..

📢 Positions within food services are an essential part of the day-to-day operations of the Correctional Service of Canada (CSC). The food services team contributes to a safer, healthier community by ensuring quality nutrition and dietary care in correctional institutions across the country. Join our dynamic team and contribute to meaningful work that makes a difference nationwide.

👩‍🍳 As a Cook’s Helper, you will support food productions by assisting with ingredient preparation, following recipes, and performing short-order cooking, such as breakfast items, sandwiches, and other hot foods. You will be helping in the production of meals, serve food while maintaining portion control, and monitor food temperatures to ensure safety and quality. You will be preparing special meals for both religious and therapeutic diets.
The role also includes assisting with ordering, receiving, storing, and distributing food supplies; maintaining inventory and secure storage areas, and supporting meal assembly and delivery to inmates, as well as the provision and distribution of rations for the SGMP (Small Group Meal Preparation) program, where inmates prepare meals independently.
You will maintain cleanliness in kitchen, dining, and storage areas, and operate a variety of kitchen equipment while reporting any issues. This includes sweeping, mopping, cleaning and sanitizing surfaces and equipment. As well you will clean and put away dishes, meal trays and kitchen utensils and equipment both by hand and through the dishwasher. A key aspect of the role is training offender workers in food preparation, service, safety procedures, and workplace behaviours to support their employability and rehabilitation. You will also ensure all activities comply with established safety, security, and fire prevention procedures and documentation of such.

title: Cabinetmaker
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Company Description
The House of Commons Administration delivers outstanding services to Members of Parliament and their employees in support of parliamentary democracy. Our success is made possible by our talented and dedicated workforce. We leverage diversity in all its forms and recognize that everyone has valuable contributions to make and the potential for individual growth. If you dream of joining an organization that is small enough for you to be noticed, but big enough to provide you with a meaningful career, then we want to hear from you!
Job Description
The House of Commons Parliamentary Precinct Operations is currently looking to staff the Cabinetmaker position.
As a Cabinetmaker, you will use your expertise in woodworking to construct, repair, and restore furniture both in the shop and on site, delivering specialized services throughout the Parliamentary Precinct. You will play an important role in conserving and restoring heritage pieces, building custom furniture, and repairing furniture, woodwork, and architectural millwork. A key aspect of this position is your ability to perform wood carving and decorative restoration work, including the reproduction, repair, and restoration of carved details on heritage furniture and architectural features while preserving their historical integrity. You will also provide specialized woodworking services to Members of Parliament, House Administration, and the Library of Parliament, and contribute to special projects and events as required. To succeed in this role, you bring demonstrated experience in wood carving, along with the craftsmanship, attention to detail, and commitment needed to preserve historically significant assets in accordance with heritage conservation standards.
This position requires extensive physical efforts and therefore, the candidates must successfully pass a pre-placement medical / physical fitness assessment.
Top Reasons to Join the Trade Services team:
By joining this team, you'll work directly with heritage and antique workpieces, equipped with a diverse range of tools and materials that will allow you to challenge yourself and thrive in your tasks. You'll be part of a collaborative, supportive team where creativity and camaraderie are celebrated. This role goes beyond traditional woodworking - it's an opportunity to work on historically significant elements. In our family-like atmosphere, you'll have the opportunity to fully express your creativity while mastering a specialized trade. Employment at Parliament opens doors for professional advancement and skill enhancement, fostering a deep sense of pride and accomplishment as a valued member of our workforce.
- Training and development opportunities.
- Work-life balance /35-hour workweek
- 4 weeks’ vacation (minimum)
Qualifications
Education :
- Post-secondary education in woodworking and a recognized cabinetmaking certification obtained through an apprenticeship program, or an equivalent combination of education, training, and experience;
- Specialized knowledge, training, and technical expertise in wood carving.
Experiences :
- Strong interpersonal skills, with the ability to build and maintain effective working relationships with clients, colleagues, and stakeholders;
- Experience in woodworking and cabinetmaking, including the application of both contemporary and heritage restoration techniques;
- Experience performing wood carving and restoration work;
- Experience in the use of various equipment and tools;
- Experience applying occupational health and safety standards, practices, and procedures in a workshop environment.
Additional Information

title: Inventory - Junior Emergency Response Advisor (Developmental)
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Level: CH-02
Who can apply: Persons residing in Canada, and Canadian citizens and Permanent residents abroad.
About the position
Duties
As a Developmental Junior Emergency Response Advisor, you will improve your skills and knowledge by undergoing a thorough developmental program.
What does ‘Developmental’ mean?
Developmental Junior Emergency Response Advisors (CH-02) are provided with on-the-job training and learning opportunities enabling them to acquire technical knowledge, and develop skills and abilities essential for promotion, generally within one year, to the position Emergency Response Advisor (CH-03).
The developmental program will gradually expose you to the day-to-day operations of the emergency centre during regular business hours. As you gain experience, you will spend time in the emergency centre under the supervision of an Emergency Response Advisor. You will also perform project support related tasks, to get a good understanding of the type of work that CANUTEC accomplishes.
Regular exercises and evaluation will gauge your progress, culminating with a final evaluation to assess your skills as an Emergency Response Advisor. Upon completion of the final evaluation, the intent is to appoint you as an Emergency Response Advisor (CH-03). In this new position, you will be required to work unsupervised shifts (day, evening, overnight and weekends) on a rotational basis as CANUTEC services are offered 24 hours a day and 365 days per year. When not scheduled in the emergency centre, Emergency Response Advisors work on various projects in a hybrid work model.
It is important to know that due to the requirement of doing shift work and travelling, you will have access to interesting benefits and premiums as well as different allowances as per the Applied Science & Patent Examination Collective Agreement.
The successful candidate is a motivated, detail- oriented multi-tasker, who has a genuine passion for science, problem-solving and helping people. They are someone who wants to invest in their career and are eager to learn. You will be trained to work on high profile and sensitive files affecting the national interests and requiring effective interpersonal skills. Some files deal with sensitive matters such as death, suicide, and self-harm. You will need to be a fast thinker to ensure quality communication with a multitude of stakeholders such as:
- First responders;
- Public safety personnel;
- Provincial spill reporting centers;
- Transport Canada internal services;
- Other government agencies;
- Shippers, carriers, and importers of dangerous goods.
Work environment
Pursue a career at the highly reputable Canadian Transport Emergency Centre (CANUTEC) at Transport Canada (TC) !
CANUTEC's mandate is to promote public safety in the transportation of dangerous goods by all modes. We are a national advisory service that operates an emergency centre remotely assisting first responders in managing dangerous goods incidents on a 24/7 basis.
CANUTEC is a team composed of about 25 employees who report to one Director. The team is divided between the CANUTEC Registration team and the Emergency Response Advisors (CH-02 and CH-03). All the Emergency Response Advisors report to two Managers, the Emergency Operations Centre Manager for their work in the emergency centre and the Research & Publishing Services Manager for their work on various projects.
One example of CANUTEC’s projects is the publication of the Emergency Response Guidebook, developed in collaboration with the US, Mexico and Argentina: https://tc.canada.ca/en/dangerous-goods/canutec/emergency-response-guidebook
At CANUTEC, we know that making the jump from a standard job in the scientific field to emergency management in government can be intimidating. Therefore, we support scientists who heed the call of the emergency world with robust, hands-on training, alongside theorical training.
Intent of the process
The intent of this continuous recruitment inventory is to create and maintain a bank of applications for future staffing needs within CANUTEC at Transport Canada in the National Capital Region. As positions are available, a pull of candidates may be conducted and candidates who meet the qualifications may be contacted for further consideration.
When a pull is conducted, a pool of qualified and/or partially qualified candidates may be established within Transport Canada in the National Capital Region and may be used to staff similar positions with various tenures, language requirements and security clearance levels.

title: Developer
description:

Developer
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
Please note that we're hiring for both level 15 positions and level 16 positions.
About the positions
We are seeking innovative and skilled Developers to join our Retail Payments Supervision team! We are a collaborative and diverse team within ITS with the mission to carry out the roadmap of an effective regulatory IT platform to meet the requirements of the Bank of Canada’s role in supervising payment service providers (PSPs) . We are also beginning work on two new mandates: Stable Coin and Consumer-driven Banking .
Lead by the Director of the Retail Payments Supervision portfolio, you will join a dynamic and highly skilled team working together to design, develop, and support our regulatory IT platform built on the Power Platform.
Further, you will have the full support of your leader and teammates to enhance your skills, experiment, and further your career through our customizable Learning & Development programs across various domains (IT, Programming, Architecture, Analytics, etc.) and relevant certifications.
What you will do As a Developer, you will be responsible for developing new features and maintaining existing components for the Bank’s RPS regulatory IT platform using the Microsoft technology stack, comprised of Power Pages (Portal), Model Driven Apps, Custom PCF controls, SharePoint, Power Automate Flows, Azure services (Function Apps, APIM) and multiple system integrations.
More specifically, you will:
- Contribute to the development of the Power Platform application and peripheral technologies
- Analyze, design and implement enhancements to meet business requirements
- Maintain collaborative relationships with internal clients and external counterparts
- Perform technical and root-cause analysis on issues and make recommendations for correction
- Create working procedures and documentation on solutions and populate knowledge databases, testing plans and results
- Apply a continuous improvement mindset, by identifying innovative ways of doing or providing services to our clients; changing or reconfiguring approaches to improve efficiency and capacity
- Ensure compliance with audit requirements during the support and maintenance of applications
- Provide second and third-line support, including evening and weekend paid overtime work, as required
What you need to succeed You have a strong attention to detail with the ability to rank tasks per priority, meet deadlines and perform multiple tasks concurrently. You also can communicate effectively and maintain co-operative working relationships with the other project members and IT teams.
In addition, you have:
- Experience developing within Dynamics 365 and Power Platform or other CRM systems
- Experience building custom APIs and Plug-ins
- Proven experience with C# programming language and .NET Framework
- Proven experience with web portal development in a Microsoft or equivalent environment
- Experience developing and maintaining HTML5, CSS, JavaScript web portal applications
- Experience working with business analysts or user experience (UX) designers to creatively translate business requirements and designs into interactive web portal functionality
- Experience and understanding of source control systems, including advanced branching and merging techniques
Nice-to-have
- Experience with Liquid or equivalent templating engine
- Experience in writing programming scripts using PowerShell
Your education and experience Your combined education and work experience demonstrate that you have the proficiencies and skills for the role. We are ideally seeking candidates with a relevant degree/diploma and 3+ years of relevant experience for the job grade 15 role and 5+ years of experience for the job grade 16 role.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. Although the position language requirement is English or French essential, we do encourage everyone to improve their second language proficiency for future career growth and to contribute towards fostering a bilingual environment.

- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Secret There will be no relocation assistance provided Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available. The official title for this position is “Developer ”
Hybrid Work Model
The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .

The Bank offers additional performance pay (3%) for those who exceed expectations. Exceptional performers who far exceed expectations may be eligible for higher performance pay. Flexible and comprehensive benefits so you can choose the level of health and dental coverage that meets your needs Extra vacation days (up to five each year) that you can purchase to add to your vacation entitlement Option to join the indexed, defined-benefit pension plan after 24 consecutive months of service

At the Canada Revenue Agency we put people first.

Business Valuator (AU0284)
Conduct independent valuations of complex securities and equity transactions by researching businesses, industries, economic conditions, and legal authorities, then applying appropriate valuation methodologies, forecasts, and risk assessments. Prepare professional valuation reports in accordance with CICBV standards, engage with taxpayers to resolve valuation issues, and contribute to organizational expertise through committees and seminars.
Income Tax Auditor (AU0143)
Conducts income tax audits of complex large businesses including corporations, partnerships, and trusts. Works independently or as a member of an integrated team, to ensure compliance with the statutes administered by the CRA.
International Tax Auditor (AU0335)
Performs audits and compliance reviews of taxpayers, large businesses and multinational corporations involving international tax issues and film industry programs(1) to ensure compliance with all statutes administered by the Agency.
Tax Avoidance Auditor (AU0239) Conducts income tax audits of domestic and international aggressive tax avoidance schemes of complex large businesses including corporations, partnerships, trusts and high wealth individuals. The Chief of Residential Housing Projects and Maintenance leads the technical team responsible for housing maintenance, capital projects, inspections, and the overall management of technical operations.

📝 Lead and oversee the development of plans, reports, and financial analyses related to asset management, Housing Services Centre (HSC) Condition Assessments, capital/recapitalization proposals, and technical services program operations.

As a Special Operating Agency reporting to the Department of National Defence (DND), CFHA contributes to the quality of life of CAF members and their families through the provision of housing services, and through the responsible and sustainable management of the Department’s housing infrastructure. We are a team of 380 federal public servants who work hard to meet the needs of the Canadian Armed Forces families living in DND housing. We have close to 230 employees at our Housing Services Centers across Canada and 150 employees at our Head Office in Ottawa.
CFHA Yellowknife is a dynamic team of 7 full-time employees. We work together to provide housing services to approximately 190 Canadian Forces and RCMP families (members and civilians). The Parliamentary Budget Office (PBO) is an independent and non-partisan entity providing stimulating and rewarding work. We offer competitive salaries, excellent benefits, and learning opportunities to support professional and career development.
The Parliamentary Budget Officer is an Officer of Parliament mandated to support Parliament by providing economic and financial analysis that supports the quality of parliamentary debate and promotes greater budget transparency and accountability. Before and during general elections, the PBO's mandate also includes estimating the cost of election proposals at the request of political parties or independent members. The PBO's mandate is set out in the Parliament of Canada Act , and employment at the PBO is governed by the Parliamentary Employment and Staff Relations Act (PESRA) . The PBO is independent of the executive branch of government.
The PBO is supported by a dynamic team of highly specialized analysts and advisors. We are currently searching for candidates to support our work as an Economic/Financial Analyst .

About the position
Duties
Registry Officers and Liaison Officers are appeal process experts that support tribunal members and parties.
Duties include but are not limited to:
• Receiving and filing documents, entering data and updating case files in a case management system
• Responding to enquiries about the process over the phone and in writing

title: Anticipatory - Detachment Services Supervisor
description:
Language requirements: English essential
Level: AS-02 - SPS-ADM-02 (RCMP Civilian Member)
Who can apply: Persons residing in Canada, and Canadian citizens and Permanent residents abroad.
About the position
Work environment
We are looking for detail-oriented professionals to provide critical administrative and operational support for our detachments. These roles are the backbone of the Southeast District office, and they ensure that financial, statistical, and records management systems run smoothly so our members can focus on their mandate for public safety. You will be required to have analytical skills with the ability to research, extract, and reconcile complex data to ensure high-quality reporting.
You will provide Financial Coordination through managing the detachment budget - coordinating estimates, recommending strategies, and reconciling financial transactions. You will also assist with our Information & Records Management by overseeing the development of statistical and narrative reports and maintain operational data across various automated systems (including PRIME and CPIC) and manual filing systems. Your role provides operational support for court liaison activities and general detachment administration. Being a stakeholder, you will liaise as a point of contact for victims, witnesses, complainants, and various government agencies (such as Correctional Services Canada and Interpol), to provide information and answer enquiries.
These positions operate in fast-paced police environments. Candidates should be comfortable managing constant interruptions and be resilient when handling unsettling or graphic crime scene reports and photographs during the transcription of court documents.
For a Public Service Employee (PSE), the Southeast District offers a unique professional environment. Due to the vast and varied geographical area, the administrative and support roles are more dynamic than in a typical urban office. You aren't just processing paperwork; you are helping manage the logistics of policing across a diverse landscape. As a result, you will have the opportunity to engage in various parts of the organization. You may find yourself coordinating with a wide range of stakeholders — from municipal governments and provincial agencies to federal partners, providing you with a much broader understanding of how the RCMP fits into the larger government framework. The Southeast District is an excellent place to build a resume. You will develop a versatile skill set in problem-solving and resource management. For a PSE, the Southeast District is a place where you can move beyond routine tasks and truly manage the business of policing. It is an ideal posting for someone who wants their administrative and operation expertise to have a visible, tangible impact on a diverse and geographically stunning region.
Person(s) will not be able to work Telework due to the nature of the duties.
Remote working is not a possibility with these position(s).

title: Analyst, Screening Clearances
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Analyst, Screening Clearances
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
In addition to the position being staffed, this competition may be used to fill similar opportunities (Regular or Term) that become available at the same job grade. If you’re interested in this type of role, we encourage you to apply.
What you will do The Security Screening and Access Programs team plays a critical role in protecting the Bank's employees, information, assets, and operations by ensuring that individuals entrusted with access to Bank facilities, information, systems, and assets meet established security requirements. The team delivers personnel security screening services that support informed decision-making while maintaining the highest standards of integrity, fairness, privacy, and security.
As a Security Screening Analyst, you will support the delivery and continuous improvement of the Bank's personnel security screening program. You will manage security screening cases, analyze information from multiple sources, provide advice to stakeholders, and support screening decisions through sound analysis, judgement, and professional recommendations.
In this role, you will:
- Manage and coordinate personnel security screening cases throughout the screening lifecycle while ensuring service standards, timelines, and quality requirements are met.
- Review, analyze, and assess information from multiple sources to support personnel security screening activities and recommendations.
- Conduct research, verification, and fact-finding activities to validate information and support security screening assessments.
- Identify issues, inconsistencies, or concerns requiring additional review, analysis, or follow-up.
- Document findings and prepare clear, concise assessments, recommendations, correspondence, and case summaries.
- Interpret and apply security screening policies, standards, procedures, and guidelines to support consistent and risk-informed decision-making.
- Provide advice, guidance, and responsive client service to hiring managers, applicants, Human Resources partners, and other stakeholders regarding security screening requirements, processes, and timelines.
- Collaborate with internal and external partners to support onboarding, offboarding, access management, and workforce security initiatives.
- Maintain accurate records and case files in accordance with privacy, information management, and security requirements.
- Monitor workload, service standards, and operational performance measures and contribute to reporting and quality assurance activities.
- Support process improvements, modernization initiatives, and technology-enabled solutions that enhance the effectiveness, efficiency, and client experience of the Bank's personnel security program.
What you need to succeed You are a highly organized and client-focused professional who exercises sound judgement and discretion when managing sensitive information. You are able to analyze information, identify key issues, and communicate recommendations clearly and effectively.
You demonstrate:
- Strong analytical and critical-thinking skills.
- Sound judgement and decision-making abilities.
- Excellent client service orientation.
- Strong interpersonal and relationship-management skills.
- Effective oral and written communication skills.
- Attention to detail and commitment to quality.
- Initiative and problem-solving abilities.
- Adaptability and flexibility in a fast-paced environment.
- The ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.
- A collaborative and team-oriented approach.
- Professionalism and discretion when handling sensitive or confidential information.
Nice-to-have The following would be considered assets:
- Experience conducting interviews, fact-finding discussions, or investigative activities.
- Experience conducting open-source research and verification activities.
- Knowledge of Government of Canada personnel security standards and practices.
- Knowledge of privacy, information-management, and security principles.
- Experience supporting operational reporting, quality assurance, or continuous improvement initiatives.
Your education and experience This position requires a university degree or college diploma in criminology, security management, intelligence studies, public administration, business administration, law, risk management, or another related discipline and a minimum of two years of relevant experience in personnel security screening, investigations, security administration, risk assessment, compliance, intelligence, human resources, law enforcement, access management, or a related field.
You must also have experience:
- Reviewing, analyzing, and synthesizing information from multiple sources.
- Preparing written assessments, reports, recommendations, briefing materials, or correspondence.
- Interpreting and applying policies, procedures, standards, directives, or regulatory requirements.
- Providing advice, guidance, or client service to internal or external stakeholders.
- Using Microsoft 365 applications and electronic information-management, workflow, or case-management systems.
Innovative Mindset We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement T he Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.
What you need to know
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents
- Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Secret
- Relocation assistance may be provided, if required
- Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.
Hybrid Work Model The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .

Did you know? As members of Translation and Editorial Services in the Communications Department, Senior Editors help the Bank of Canada achieve its policy and public communication objectives by ensuring that high-profile publications are clear, coherent, accessible and effective for their intended audiences.
The work of language professionals is evolving rapidly, especially in light of new technologies. The successful candidate will need to combine language expertise with solid skills in project management, relationship management, digital literacy and artificial intelligence. The successful candidate is innovative and has a continuous-improvement mindset.
What you will do Reporting to the Director, Translation and Editorial Services, you will:
Editing
- edit a wide range of English texts for clarity, accuracy, consistency and impact, adapting the level and type of edit to the product, audience and communication risk
- provide substantive, structural, stylistic and copy editing, including significant rewriting when needed to strengthen logic, flow, voice, tone and accessibility, particularly for complex economic content
- work with authors to clarify objectives, refine key messages and narrative, anticipate how audiences will interpret the content, reduce the risk of misinterpretation and apply Bank style standards and editorial practices consistently
- contribute to developing, maintaining and applying Bank style standards, writing guidance and editorial practices to ensure they meet the organization’s evolving needs
Project management
- plan, coordinate and deliver complex, high-profile editorial projects by defining milestones, responsibilities and deadlines, monitoring progress and identifying issues early
- develop effective work strategies, adjust priorities as operational needs, deadlines or scope change, and keep projects moving by considering the timelines, constraints and communication needs of the teams involved
Relationship management and influence
- build trusted working relationships with internal clients, including with senior management, by understanding their objectives, audiences, constraints and expectations
- promote effective collaboration among stakeholders in complex projects by clarifying expectations, facilitating communication, helping to resolve differing points of view and communicating thoughtfully under tight timelines and high expectations
Digital literacy and artificial intelligence
- use technology, including artificial intelligence tools, critically, safely and responsibly by evaluating outputs, confidentiality risks and the value it adds to editorial work
- help integrate technological tools into the team’s work by participating in trials, making recommendations and sharing best practices
Continuous improvement and innovation
- recommend practical improvements to processes, tools, editorial practices and ways of working to increase efficiency, consistency and quality
- stay informed about trends in editing, plain language, communications and related technologies, and help turn new ideas into team practices, guidelines and internal standards
What you need to succeed You have a strong understanding of economics and a genuine interest in the subject, enabling you to work confidently with complex economic content and engage meaningfully with authors and subject matter experts.
You bring demonstrated expertise in substantive, structural, stylistic and copy editing, proofreading and project management. You can apply plain-language principles, edit for the web and advise on structure, narrative, tone and audience needs. You are an adaptable, collaborative language advisor who can explain editorial recommendations clearly, build consensus, identify communication risks and opportunities for improvement, and deliver high-quality advice and content within prescribed time frames.
Nice-to-have
- academic background in economics
- education or training in translation and experience translating from French to English
Your education and experience This position requires a bachelor’s degree in English, journalism or a related field and 7 to 10 years of experience editing complex, high-profile communications and research publications. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Innovative Mindset We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement T he Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.

- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents
- Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Secret
- Relocation assistance may be provided, if required
- Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.
Hybrid Work Model The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .

About the position
Duties
The Housing Projects and Maintenance Technician is part of the technical team responsible for inspections, maintenance coordination, and the overall upkeep of the housing portfolio.
Duties of the position includes, but are not limited to:
• Identify, assess and document repair and maintenance requirements for CFHA housing units.
• Plan, organize and implement repair and maintenance work on CFHA housing units through service providers. This would include the preparation of repair and maintenance work orders.
• Oversee and confirm work/repair completion in accordance with the terms of the contract, specifications, technical codes and standards.
• Conduct responsive and preventive repair and maintenance inspections of housing units and equipment/systems.
• Provide customer services that includes responding to CFHA housing unit service requests, elaborating repair and maintenance plans/schedules on the housing units.
• Provide ongoing instruction, information and guidance to service providers, team members, and housing unit occupants.
• Assess and perform minor repair/installation and/or temporary fixes/solutions. This would include identifying and utilizing materials and tools required to complete the repairs.
• Prepare technical documentation and plans, provide coordination, collaboration and support for capital asset project design, development and implementation through external service providers.
• Maintain ongoing assessment and provide technical inputs with respect to housing unit operations, repairs, life cycle replacement, betterment projects and activities.
Work environment
A LITTLE SOMETHING ABOUT CFHA...
As a Special Operating Agency reporting to the Department of National Defence (DND), CFHA contributes to the quality of life of CAF members and their families through the provision of housing services, and through the responsible and sustainable management of the Department's housing infrastructure. We are a team of 380 federal public servants who work hard to meet the needs of the Canadian Armed Forces families living in DND housing. We have close to 230 employees at our Housing Services Centers across Canada and 150 employees at our Head Office in Ottawa.
CFHA Yellowknife is a dynamic team of 7 full-time employees. We work together to provide housing services to approximately 190 Canadian Forces and RCMP families (members and civilians). As a CFHA employee, you will play an important role in the implementation of housing services while working with a dedicated team. If you enjoy new and rewarding challenges, apply today!

The immediate need is to staff one English Essential position on a permanent basis at the CFHA Yellowknife (NT) location. A pool will be established and may be used to staff future positions at the CFHA Yellowknife location, including both permanent and temporary positions.

title: Senior Project Manager (#24799)
description:
Language requirements: English essential
Defence Industrial Strategy
The NRC has an important role within the Government of Canada's Defence Industrial Strategy, accelerating research and innovation, and helping Canadian businesses develop leading-edge technologies for civilian and military use.
With expertise across fields such as transportation, quantum science, medical countermeasures and advanced manufacturing, the NRC is hiring to drive the development of national sovereign defence capabilities. The following role will support the NRC’s contributions to defence priorities.
The role
The NRC is building new capabilities to help Canada accelerate the development, integration and adoption of emerging drone, counter-drone and autonomous systems technologies. At the centre of this effort is the Drone Innovation Hub (DIH) and its Aurora Shield program—bringing together NRC researchers, engineers and facilities with the Canadian Armed Forces, Department of National Defence, industry, academia and other partners to tackle some of Canada's most important defence and security technology challenges.
We are looking for a Senior Project Manager to help turn that ambition into action .
Working alongside the Aurora Shield Program Director, the successful candidate will help shape and deliver a rapidly growing portfolio of research, technology development and innovation activities. This is not a traditional project management role. Individual projects are led by researcher and engineer Project Managers from across the NRC; the Senior Project Manager will work across those projects—helping PMs succeed, maintaining coherence across the portfolio, solving problems and ensuring that the program delivers as a whole.
The role also extends beyond the individual projects. Aurora Shield is developing new ways for NRC, DND, the Canadian Armed Forces and industry to work together, including major ecosystem wide initiatives. The successful candidate will help take these initiatives from ambitious concepts to executable activities—working through the plans, partnerships, budgets, documentation and details required to make them real.
The result is a role with an unusually broad range: from strategy to execution, and from individual projects to the broader Canadian defence innovation ecosystem . On any given day, the Senior Project Manager might help a Project Manager resolve a delivery challenge, work through program budgets and priorities, develop the implementation plan for a new Aurora Shield initiative, prepare material for senior decision-makers, or engage with DND, other government departments and Canadian industry and academia.
We are looking for someone who thrives in that environment—someone who can bring structure to complexity, move comfortably between technical and programmatic discussions, build relationships across organizations, and turn good ideas into delivered outcomes. The Senior Project Manager would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Bachelor or Master’s Degree in engineering management, systems engineering, engineering, business/project management or related discipline.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency

- Significant* experience managing complex, multi-disciplinary projects or programs involving science, engineering, technology development or innovation;
- Significant* experience working with multi-disciplinary teams of engineers, scientists, technical specialists, project managers and/or business professionals;
- Significant* experience in program or project management, including planning, budgeting, scheduling, risk management, reporting and delivery;
- Experience coordinating a portfolio of related projects or activities and identifying dependencies, risks and opportunities across multiple projects;
- Experience developing detailed implementation plans, project documentation, business cases, proposals, plans or similar products from higher-level concepts or strategic direction; and
- Experience engaging and coordinating with multiple internal and external stakeholders.
Assets:
- Experience in aerospace, defence and security, autonomous systems, drones or other complex technology-development environments;
- Experience working with the Department of National Defence, Canadian Armed Forces, other government departments or the Canadian defence industry;
- Experience with intellectual property, collaborative research agreements, contracting, procurement or other mechanisms supporting complex research and development activities.
*Significant experience is referring to between 2 to 6 years.

For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.

Technical competencies

- Ability to translate strategic objectives and emerging concepts into structured plans, requirements, activities and executable projects;
- Ability to support and enable technical Project Managers while maintaining visibility and coherence across a broader program;
- Ability to analyze complex technical, programmatic and organizational issues, identify practical solutions and drive issues toward resolution;
- Ability to communicate complex technical and program information effectively amongst teams, organizations and stakeholders with varying levels of familiarity with the domain;
- Ability to develop high-quality plans, briefing materials, decision documents, proposals and other written products for technical and senior audiences;
- Ability to establish and maintain productive relationships with government, industry, academic and other external stakeholders; and

NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey.
