Work environment
The students will work on multi-model data evaluation and analysis in the context of the Task Force on Hemispheric Transport of Air Pollution (HTAP, htap.org). HTAP is an international scientific cooperative effort to improve the understanding of intercontinental transport of air pollution. HTAP3 multi-model experiments, include “OPNS” on ozone, particulate matter, and deposition, and “Fires” on multi-pollutant wildfire impacts. The students will download and analyze model output and measurements from several sources using ECCC’s supercomputer resources. They will compare atmospheric model output to several measurement-based datasets to determine model performance of air pollutant distributions and related variables. They will also intercompare models’ future projections of air pollution under various scenarios, and come to conclusions related to model performance, reasons for model biases, suggestions for improvement, and degree of confidence in model predictions.

About CSE
The Communications Security Establishment (CSE) is Canada’s agency responsible for foreign signals intelligence, cyber operations and cyber security. Learn more about our mission , and what it means to work in a security and intelligence field .
CSE is committed to fostering a culture of equity, diversity and inclusion. This isn’t just an ideal, it’s crucial to our mission. Find out about our workplace culture , including our diversity and inclusion initiatives.
Become part of our team and you’ll understand why CSE is the most important organization you’ve never heard of (YouTube) .
Job summary
CSE is currently looking for systems administrators and desktop administrators from a diverse range of technical backgrounds who will thrive working on unique problems in an open minded and innovative environment, and who value the different perspectives of others. We are looking for people who constantly strive for better solutions to keep our country safe, who seek to learn more about the cyber challenges that impact us, and who collaborate with partners, colleagues, and teams on complex problems. You should be someone who enjoys a challenging career and who desires to learn new technologies to expand and evolve your expertise.
Our positions exist in very dynamic and unique operational environments and provides direct support to CSE missions. We are a unique technical organization with hundreds of subject matter experts across IT domains. We have guilds of expertise who collaborate in agency, government, and international initiatives to find the right solution to complex problems. Individuals selected will assist with the engineering, configuration, and support of a variety of hardware and software. Our team relies heavily on virtualization to support our operations.
Your work will have a significant impact on Canada’s security posture and will contribute towards ensuring the safety of Canadians. Your role will entail technical research and development, enabling continued innovation within various IT environments. You will be responsible for effective provisioning, installation, configuration and supporting advancement of many technologies across multiple IT domains while adhering to ITIL principles.
You may work with many common enterprise services: Linux and/or Windows, data storage & protection services, scripting, and networking. You may also be exposed to cloud services, cryptography, PKI, the system development lifecycle, and automation technologies.
The intent of this selection process is to staff various entry-level, intermediate and senior positions across different activity areas of CSE. This selection process will be used to recruit three streams :
Stream 1: Systems Administrator
As a systems administrator, you will work to support critical infrastructure with unique challenges using the latest technologies.
Stream 2: Desktop Administrator
As a desktop administrator, you will support various endpoint solutions (mobility, local, VDI) and engage in critical projects with unique challenges using the latest technologies.
Stream 3: Other Specialties
CSE is looking for various specialists in multiple IT domains (for example, but not limited to: storage, monitoring, Citrix, AV/VTC, telephony, VMWare). Where a system administrator would typically have a broader range of experience, a specialist has more depth within an area of expertise.

For bilingual positions, second language evaluations will be offered to candidates who don’t have valid language test results issued by the Government of Canada.

title: Junior Research Officer, High Temperature Materials (#25914)
description:
Language requirements: English essential
The role
We are looking for a vibrant and dynamic Junior Researcher to support our High Temperature Materials team within the Aerospace Research Centre. The Junior Researcher would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect, and Creativity.
The primary responsibility of the Junior Researcher is to develop and apply, in collaboration with internal and external partners, predictive models including machine learning (ML), materials thermodynamics, etc. for high-throughput identification and screening of advanced materials for gas turbine engine applications. The Junior Researcher will be expected to think critically and creatively develop innovative solutions and approaches using modern ML methods and identify opportunities to adopt this technology into various research projects within the High Temperature Materials team. The Junior Researcher is also be expected to contribute to design, synthesis, processing, and characterization of the microstructures and thermal-mechanical properties of advanced high-temperature materials. The Junior Researcher works in a team environment with researchers and technical experts in world-class facilities. Activities also include the development of proposals for new research initiatives, project management, and providing service to NRC clients. The Junior Researcher provides input into the overall direction and research priorities for the program area within the context of the Portfolio business plan.
You will collaborate directly with senior personnel, other project managers and external clients.This position will appeal to a person who is well organized, who is detail-oriented, and who enjoys working as part of a multidisciplinary team to deliver excellent service.
If you’re that person, then this may be the perfect role for you!
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
M.A.Sc. or Ph.D. in materials science, aerospace engineering, or a related field with a focus on high temperature materials and application of digital tools such as machine learning for accelerated materials discovery and phase/property prediction.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Demonstrated experience in the research and development of advanced materials, particularly those used as high temperature materials in gas turbine engine applications;
- Demonstrated experience with the safe operation of a metallographic laboratory for the purposes of microstructural characterization, including the use of metallographic preparation equipment, chemicals, optical and scanning electron microscopy;
- Demonstrated experience in applying machine learning algorithms and techniques to materials science problems, including supervised and unsupervised learning, deep learning, and reinforcement learning;
- Experience with data preprocessing, model evaluation, handling large datasets, including data collection, cleaning, storage, and management;
- Experience with integration of computational results with machine learning models to predict material properties and behavior;
- Experience in statistical analysis and data visualization to interpret and communicate findings effectively; and
- Experience working with interdisciplinary teams, including materials scientists, engineers, data scientists, and industry stakeholders.
Assets:
- Experience in the operation of servo-hydraulic test equipment and software, particularly from MTS, and high temperature hardware such as furnaces, vacuum furnaces, and thermocouples;
- Experience in business development, marketing activities, and/or the development of partnerships and collaborations;
- Experience in the full spectrum of research activities including identification of research requirements, proposal writing, project management, data production and analysis, and reporting through written documentation, presentations, and publishing.
Condition of employment
- Secret clearance
A thorough security clearance process will be applied.
For a Secret Clearance, verification of background information over a period of 10 years is required. Individuals must have lived in Canada for a sufficient period of time to enable the security screening process.
- Must be able to work in conditions found in an ordinary laboratory environment with some (minimal) exposure to hazardous materials or chemicals such as adhesives and cleaning agents. Independently work in such environments in a safe manner, with a working-level tolerance to a typical test environment with enhanced noise levels, heat and reduced air quality; and
- Ability to hearing mechanical problems.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Basic knowledge of machine learning techniques as applied to high-throughput materials research and development;
- Advanced knowledge of materials properties, behavior, and performance, especially those relevant to gas turbine applications such as high specific strength, thermal stability and resistance to fatigue, corrosion and creep;
- Basic knowledge of relevant programming languages used in machine learning;
- Basic understanding of aerospace industry requirements and standards, including the specific challenges and constraints related to materials used in gas turbine applications;
- Solid understanding of methods used for materials synthesis, processing, and characterization of microstructure and mechanical properties for advanced high temperature materials;
- Demonstrated ability to publish research results in peer-reviewed journals; and
- Demonstrated ability to present complex technical information clearly and concisely to both technical and non-technical audiences.
Asset :
- Solid knowledge on the operation of high temperature equipment and servo-hydraulic test machines;
- Ability to manage research projects, including planning, execution, monitoring progress, work within timelines and budgets, and to adapt to changing project requirements.
Behavioural competencies
- Research - Creative thinking (Level 1)
- Research - Communication (Level 2)
- Research - Continuous professional learning (Level 1)
- Research - Initiative (Level 1)
- Research - Teamwork (Level 2)
Competency Profile(s)
For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Research
View all competency profiles
Compensation
The intent of this hiring action is to staff this position at the JRO to AsRO level, which is an intermediate to senior-career level position with a salary range of $64,739 to $116,641 .
NOTE: Please note that the full RO/RCO salary scale has five levels. Salary determination will be based on a review of the candidate’s expertise, outcomes and impacts of their previous work experience relative to the requirements of the level. As such, the initial salary could be within another level of the RO/RCO salary scale (i.e. above or below the intended level for this position).
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.
Notes

title: Senior Power Electronics Researcher (#25901)
description:
Language requirements: English essential
The role
We are looking for a Senior Power Electronics Researcher to support our e-Auto Challenge Program hosted by the Automotive and Surface Transportation (AST) Research Centre. The successful candidate would be someone who shares our core values of Integrity, Excellence, Respect and Creativity.
The e Auto Challenge Program aims to strengthen the competitiveness of Canadian auto industry on the world stage by accelerating and de-risking novel Canadian Zero Emissions Vehicle (ZEV) solutions innovation. Specifically, this initiative focuses on advancing, integrating and deploying advanced power electronics technologies for inverter, converter, and controller applications to enable higher power density, more efficiency, reliable and lower cost traction drives, battery systems, and charging infrastructures.
The Senior Power Electronics Researcher is a technical leader who will play a key role in shaping and delivering the Power Electronics theme for the e-Auto Challenge program, bridging advanced research with product ready solutions in collaboration with multidisciplinary teams across industry, academia and government to achieve technical excellence and commercial success.
This position calls for a visionary researcher with demonstrated expertise in automotive power electronics development, system integration and validation for industrial applications.
The activities in support of program area objectives may include:
- Research and Development: Conduct cutting-edge research in advanced power electronics technologies for inverter, converter, and controller applications related to zero-emission vehicles (ZEV).
- Experimental Design and Execution: Design and execute novel experiments to assess feasibility of cyber-physical systems, introduce or improve instrumentation and data collection, and validate applications for machine learning.
- Technology Assessment: Evaluate emerging technologies, instrumentation devices and other tools related to power electronics for electric vehicles applications.
- Collaboration: Collaborate with cross-functional teams to support interdisciplinary research projects.
- Documentation and Reporting: Prepare technical reports, presentations, and publications for internal and external stakeholders.
- Intellectual Property (IP): Contribute to the development and protection of IP through invention disclosures, patent applications, and technology transfer activities.
- Continuous Learning: Stay current to trends in metal additive manufacturing through conferences and professional development activities.
- Client Engagement: Support the business development function as a scientific discipline leader. Assist in identifying client requirements and prepare technical scope of project proposals.
Screening criteria
Applicants must demonstrate within the content of their application that they meet the following screening criteria in order to be given further consideration as candidates:
Education
Ph.D. in Electrical Engineering, Power Electronics, or a field relevant to the position. A Master’s Degree in Engineering combined with experience in research or technology development relevant to the position may also be considered.
For information on certificates and diplomas issued abroad, please see Degree equivalency
Experience
- Extensive** and recent*** experience in the design, architecture and implementation of high power, high efficiency inverter, converter or controller topologies using Silicon carbide (SiC) and Gallium Nitride (GaN) technologies.
- Significant* experience in systems-level electrical, mechanical, and thermal interfaces optimization to meet performance, cost, and manufacturability targets.
- Significant* experience in switching behavior, losses, and electromagnetic interference mitigation strategies for high frequency operation.
- Significant* experience in developing compact, thermally robust packaging solutions for high-voltage automotive environments.
- Significant* experience in design-for-reliability, design-for-manufacturing, and cost optimization practices.
- Significant* experience leading and delivering research projects.
The following experience criterion would be considered an asset:
- Experience working in an industrial research and development (R&D), product development and/or product deployment environment within the automotive, clean tech or defence sector.
* Significant experience is defined as experience of three (3) to six (6) years. ** Extensive experience is defined as experience of at least seven (7) years. *** Recent experience is defined as experience acquired within the last two (2) years.
Condition of employment
Reliability Status For a Reliability Status, verification of background information over a period of 5 years is required.
Language requirements
English
Information on language requirements and self-assessment tests
Assessment criteria
Candidates will be assessed on the basis of the following criteria:
Technical competencies
- Expert knowledge in the design of power converters and multi-level inverters for electric vehicle (EV) powertrain and charging systems.
- Expert knowledge of SiC and GaN devices multi-physics application for high power-density design.
- Solid knowledge of high-voltage design, insulation coordination, dielectric materials, creepage/clearance, and partial discharge phenomena.
- Solid knowledge of electromagnetic compatibility, electromagnetic interference mitigation, and automotive electromagnetic compatibility standards compliance.
- Solid knowledge of motor control integration, drivetrain efficiency, and system-level architecture of EV powertrains.
- Knowledge of project management principles and practices.
Behavioural competencies
- Research - Communication (Level 2)
- Research - Creative thinking (Level 3)
- Research - Partnering (Level 2)
- Research - Results orientation (Level 3)
- Research - Teamwork (Level 2)

For this position, the NRC will evaluate candidates using the following competency profile: Research .
View all competency profiles
Compensation
The intent of this hiring action is to staff this position at the AsRO/AcRO level, which is an early-career level position with a salary range of $83,985 to $139,608 .
NOTE: Please note that the full RO/RCO salary scale has five levels. Salary determination will be based on a review of the candidate’s expertise, outcomes and impacts of their previous work experience relative to the requirements of the level. As such, the initial salary could be within another level of the RO/RCO salary scale (i.e. above or below the intended level for this position).
NRC employees enjoy a wide-range of competitive benefits including a robust pension plan, comprehensive health and dental coverage, disability and life insurance, office closure at the end of December, and additional supports to enhance your well-being throughout your career and beyond.
Discover the possible
Anything is possible at the NRC, named in 2026 one of Canada’s Top Employers for Young People, Top Employer in the National Capital Region and Forbes Canada’s Best Employers!
As Canada’s largest research and innovation organization, our world-renowned research pushes the boundaries of science and engineering to make the impossible, possible. Every day we explore new ideas through innovative research and help companies discover possibilities that impact Canada’s future and the world.
At the NRC, you’ll also discover new possibilities. Our supportive workplace fosters a culture of creativity, welcoming fresh perspectives and innovation at all levels. We value teamwork. You’ll collaborate across multiple fields and with the brightest minds to find creative solutions. Most importantly, you’ll discover what’s possible within you as you grow, make valuable contributions and progress in your professional journey. From ground-breaking discoveries to a life-changing career, discover your possible at the NRC.

Duties
The Directorate of Architecture and Engineering Services (DAES) provides specialized technical expertise, technical authority, and professional advice in support of the planning, delivery, operation, maintenance, renewal, recapitalization, and stewardship of Defence infrastructure.
Within DAES, Architecture provides architectural leadership, technical authority, oversight, and strategic advice to help ensure Defence facilities are functional, mission-ready, resilient, secure, inclusive, sustainable, durable, and aligned with operational requirements.

It is an opportunity to apply professional judgement and architectural expertise where they can have significant impact: reviewing and advising on major capital projects; identifying risks and opportunities; interpreting policy and standards; supporting governance and quality assurance; developing technical requirements and guidance; and providing decision support throughout the infrastructure lifecycle from planning and design through delivery, operation, maintenance, renewal, recapitalization, and disposal.

About the position
Duties
Shape the Future of Policing Through Strategic Policy Leadership
Reporting to the Deputy Chief, Corporate Policy Branch, Planning Sector, you will join a small, high-performing team of policy professionals serving as the organization's centre of expertise for corporate policy development. This is a unique opportunity to influence organizational direction, drive modernization, and contribute directly to the strategic evolution of the Service.
In this role, you will lead complex policy initiatives that support organizational excellence, operational effectiveness, and informed decision-making across the Service.
Key responsibilities include:
• Lead the development, review, modernization, and maintenance of corporate policies and related policy instruments that support organizational priorities and operational excellence.
• Collaborate with managers, senior leaders, subject matter experts, clients, and external partners to ensure policies are practical, aligned, and responsive to business and operational needs.
• Design and maintain policy frameworks, governance processes, and policy instruments that advance strategic objectives and strengthen organizational accountability.
• Prepare and present strategic products, including policies, briefing notes, executive reports, presentations, and consultation materials for senior leadership and decision-makers.
• Develop and implement policy rollout strategies, including communications, training, workshops, toolkits, and awareness initiatives to support successful adoption across the organization.
• Provide expert policy advice and guidance while building strong stakeholder relationships, participating in policy governance activities, and enhancing employee access to policy resources and tools.
Why Join Us?
This role offers the opportunity to influence corporate decision-making, contribute to organizational modernization, and work on initiatives that have a lasting impact across the Service. You will collaborate with leaders at all levels, tackle complex policy challenges, and help shape the frameworks that guide the organization's future.

It has its own classification, compensation system, and staffing regime. The security screening process involves a comprehensive background investigation to assess the candidate’s reliability, honesty, trustworthiness, loyalty to Canada and reliability as it relates to that loyalty. This security screening investigation includes, but is not limited to, a loyalty assessment, law enforcement verifications, financial verifications, internet inquiries, as well as personal and employment reference checks. Candidates will also be required to participate in a security screening interview, which will cover a range of topics needed to complete the security screening assessment.
Candidates should be aware that participation in, or completion of, the recruitment process does not guarantee eligibility for a PPS security screening. Security screening is conducted as a separate process, and the outcome may be influenced by several factors, including the length of time an individual has resided in Canada and the resulting ability to verify required background information.
Interactions with law enforcement, credit history, personal associations, and other relevant security considerations may also affect a candidate’s eligibility to be granted the required security screening level and may influence the time needed to complete the security screening process.

employer: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
description:
Language requirements: English essential
Level: SG-PAT-03
Who can apply: Persons residing in Canada, and Canadian citizens and Permanent residents abroad.
About the position
Work environment
As a Patent Examiner you will read and analyze inventions described in patent applications. Check out the Canadian Patents Database to have a glimpse of what a patent application looks like. You will search technical databases to ascertain how the invention differs from the state of the art. You will communicate with the applicant, mainly via written reports, outlining your analysis and whatever defects need to be corrected before approving the patent.
The SG-PAT-03 level is a training level in preparation for advancement to the SG-PAT-04 working level for Patent Examiners after a 2-year period (SG-PAT-04 salary from $101,393 to $124,188). You will learn both the technical and legal aspects of patent examination in a comprehensive training program comprising virtual classroom courses and on-the-job practical training under the guidance of a Senior Patent Examiner who will help you become proficient in the art of patent examination. Patent examiners may be required to work on a variety of patent applications from any technology area relevant to the Mechanical Division.
While a certain proportion of patent applications the Office receives is in French, the language used for the majority of the patent applications, our examination reports, and most of our literature searches, is English, so the ability to understand and communicate in English is essential. Regardless, CIPO is a bilingual organization which fosters the use of both French and English, and as such you can expect to work in a bilingual work environment which includes among other things, bilingual documentation and internal work tools, as well as on-the-job training and interacting with your manager in the official language of your choice. For those who are officially bilingual (as established by language testing), you may have the opportunity to examine a proportion of your workload in French. Company Description
The Library of Parliament is a non-partisan organization that provides a unique and stimulating work environment. We are led by our guiding principles of agility, collaboration, excellence, impartiality, and inclusion. Job Description
Reporting to a Manager, Branches and Parliamentary Outreach, the Research Technician or the Technician, Information Service is responsible for providing non-partisan, confidential and bilingual general reference, instruction and information services to parliamentarians, authorized clients and the general public on a wide variety of topics and issues of interest.
The incumbent performs the following duties:
- Reference interviews in person, on the telephone and virtually to properly define clients’ requests, needs and deadlines.
- Searches, selects and retrieves information by using a range of Library resources in order to respond effectively to clients’ requests.
- Provides instruction to clients in using parliamentary publications on the web and the Library’s electronic or print collections, and on Library services and products.
- Provides reference and information service support to and collaborates with colleagues in other service points of the Library, such as the Library Branches and Information Service, as may be necessary in order to ensure appropriate levels of service and support to clients.

Knowledge :

About the Role
Under the direct supervision of the Manager, Human Resources, the Senior Human Resources Advisor serves as a trusted advisor that, through the building and nurturing of credible, collaborative, value-driven relationships, provides consultative and advisory services to support, guide and enable management and staff on a full range of talent management matters, including the interpretation and application of the collective agreement/terms and conditions of employment, related legislations as well as policies, procedures, guidelines and employment related issues. The Advisor serves as the first point of contact for labour/employee relations issues and supports the grievance process, investigations, and implementation of disciplinary actions, as required. The incumbent participates in labour-management meetings and supports preparation for bargaining, as needed.
The Advisor is the primary liaison and point of contact between People and Organizational Culture and the rest of the organization and contributes to achieving functional and organizational results. While the role supports specific divisions/sections, the Advisor brings a Council-wide perspective—contributing to, promoting and delivering strategies, programs, initiatives, policies, procedures and best practices that advance Council’s strategic human resources plan and objectives. The incumbent pivots seamlessly demonstrates agility between strategic orientation, operational delivery, and the development of creative solutions to meet the evolving needs of Council’s talent management.
The Advisor also assists in defining, capturing, tracking and reporting talent management analytics. The incumbent contributes to continuous improvement initiatives, provides presentations to various audiences, prepares reports on matters related to talent management and performs other related duties.

title: Analyst, Cyber Assurance
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Analyst, Cyber Assurance
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
In addition to the position being staffed, this competition may be used to fill similar opportunities (Regular or Term) that become available at the same job grade. If you’re interested in this type of role, we encourage you to apply.
Why join us
You will join an innovative and collaborative team helping shape the future of IT security at Canada’s central bank. You will have opportunities to exercise judgement, work with enterprise cyber security tools, deepen your knowledge across assurance domains, and grow through the Bank’s learning and development programs.
About the position
Join the Cyber Security Assurance team and help connect people, information and assurance activities in a way that supports clear decisions and effective follow-through. In this role, you will help make cyber assurance information easier to understand, monitor and act on across teams.
You will work closely with ITS portfolios to anticipate demand, align assurance activities with portfolio roadmaps, strengthen risk monitoring, coordinate follow-up on outstanding items, and communicate results to a broad range of stakeholders. This role is well suited to a dynamic communicator who enjoys building partnerships, working with data, and bringing structure to complex, cross-functional work.
Candidates with transferable strengths in communication, analysis, stakeholder engagement, project coordination or risk management are encouraged to apply. Cyber experience is valuable, but curiosity, sound judgement, attention to detail and a strong desire to learn are equally important.
What you will do
- Build trusted partnerships with ITS and business portfolios to understand priorities, project roadmaps and readiness for cyber assurance activities.
- Maintain and improve assurance and risk dashboards, KPIs, KRIs and reporting views that communicate the status of assurance activities, documented remediation updates and portfolio follow-up.
- Monitor the quality, consistency, timeliness and completeness of risk data, identify gaps, trends or overdue items, and coordinate follow-up with ITS portfolios and accountable stakeholders.
- Track decisions, action items, dependencies and remediation commitments to help ensure portfolio updates are current, clear and ready for governance or executive reporting.
- Prepare clear reports, presentations, briefing materials and awareness communications for operational teams, risk stakeholders, cyber colleagues and governance forums.
- Explain how risk assessment processes, cyber testing, vulnerability management, and third-party risk activities support and connect to the ITS project lifecycle.
- Support recurring portfolio reviews and governance discussions by helping clarify priorities, roles, responsibilities, decisions, action items and escalation paths.
- Maintain risk records, exceptions, remediation updates, follow-up notes and supporting evidence in ServiceNow IRM and related assurance tools, ensuring information remains current and ready for reporting.
- Support continuous improvement of tools and practices for planning, risk management, monitoring, reporting and governance across assurance activities.
- Maintain long-term relationships with internal and external stakeholders while contributing to a collaborative, learning-focused team environment.
What you need to succeed
You are an effective and adaptable communicator who can make complex information clear, relevant and actionable for different audiences. You combine analytical thinking, attention to detail and strong relationship skills, and you are comfortable bringing structure to evolving information, competing priorities and cross-functional work.
- Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to prepare clear briefings, reports, presentations, dashboards and awareness materials for a range of technical and non-technical audiences.
- Ability to build productive relationships, influence without direct authority, and follow up effectively with portfolio teams, project teams and risk stakeholders.
- Experience working with data to monitor status, identify trends, flag gaps or overdue items, support decisions and communicate an evidence-based story.
- Understanding of risk assessment and risk management concepts, including monitoring, reporting, remediation tracking, escalation and follow-up.
- Strong organizational, coordination and problem-solving skills, with the ability to manage competing demands, track commitments, maintain accurate information and drive timely follow-up with appropriate independence.
- Knowledge of the IT project lifecycle and how governance, risk and assurance activities support delivery.
- A collaborative mindset, sound judgement, curiosity, attention to detail and a commitment to learning and continuous improvement.
Nice to have
- Experience in cyber security, technology risk, operational risk, assurance, audit, governance or a related field.
- Experience building dashboards, KPIs, KRIs or management reporting using risk, performance or portfolio data.
- Experience with ServiceNow IRM, GRC or other workflow, reporting or risk management tools.
- Experience in project coordination, portfolio support or working directly with project managers and technology delivery teams.
Your education and experience
Your combined education and work experience demonstrate that you have the competencies and skills required for the position. We are ideally seeking candidates with a degree or diploma in a relevant discipline, such as computer science, information systems, cyber security, risk management, business, communications or data analytics, together with three or more years of relevant experience. An equivalent combination of education and experience may be considered.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.
What you need to know
- Priority will be given to Canadian citizens and permanent residents Security level required: Be eligible to obtain Secret There will be no relocation assistance provided Please save a copy of the job poster. Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available.
Hybrid Work Model
The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.
What you can expect from us This is a great opportunity to join a leading organization and be part of a high-performing team. We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .
- Salaries are based on qualifications and experience and typically range from $94,193 to $110,816 (job grade 16) The Bank offers an incentive for successfully meeting expectations at 5 to 7% of your base salary. The Bank offers additional performance pay (3%) for those who exceed expectations. Exceptional performers who far exceed expectations may be eligible for higher performance pay. Flexible and comprehensive benefits so you can choose the level of health and dental coverage that meets your needs Extra vacation days (up to five each year) that you can purchase to add to your vacation entitlement Option to join the indexed, defined-benefit pension plan after 24 consecutive months of service
We wish to thank all applicants for their interest and effort in applying for this position. Only candidates selected for interviews will be contacted.

description:

About the position
Duties
Registered Nurses or Registered Psychiatric Nurses work in health clinics located within our federal institutions. Nurses provide care specializing in services that reflect the needs of a diverse patient population. As regulated (licenced) providers, nurses practice in accordance with professional standards and departmental/ institutional policy.
Care may include services targeted at:
• Opioid agonist treatment
• Emergency care
• Infectious disease prevention and treatment
• Mental health care and treatment
• Interventions to preserve life and prevent serious bodily harm
• Discharge planning
As a Nurse, you will provide patients with:
• Essential health care
• Reasonable access to non-essential health care
• Contribute to patient rehabilitation and successful reintegration into the community
• Work closely with the interdisciplinary team of professionals to improve the lives of patients
Work environment
The Correctional Service of Canada (CSC) hires skilled nurses from all backgrounds and areas of expertise. With the current health challenges facing our offender population, there is a need to recruit more nurses into our organization.
Nurses at CSC play an important role in providing quality care to approximately 15,000 offenders incarcerated in Canada's federal institutions, they work in accredited facilities. In their daily work, nurses in CSC care for offenders by contributing to the prevention, care, treatment, and support of acute and chronic physical and mental health conditions. The care provided by nurses assists in maintaining the safety of Canadians by helping to improve offender health and reintegration into the community. CSC nurses provide a wide range of clinical services that can be found in a community setting, while focusing on services that reflect the needs of the offender population.
We encourage diversity and we welcome you to apply.
Intent of the process
📌 The selection process is intended to create an inventory of qualified candidates to support staffing needs. CSC will review applications received on a regular basis and contact applicants based on the needs of the institutions. It is therefore important that you indicate all the locations where you want to work.
📌The placement of CSC employees with an affected status* as a result of a current or future workforce adjustment exercise may be considered ahead of other candidates for a deployment or an appointment. * Affected status as defined in the Workforce Adjustment Directive or appendix to the relevant collective agreement.

When you apply to this selection process, you are not applying for a specific job, but to an inventory for future vacancies. As positions become available, applicants who meet the qualifications may be contacted for further assessment.
If you apply to this process and participate in our various (NU-HOS-03) selection processes advertised in different regions, please note that you may be assessed once, and your assessment results may be applied to all of those selection processes. The waiting period for reassessment is 180 calendar days from your last assessment.
Persons are entitled to participate in the appointment process in the official language of their choice.
The Public Service Resourcing System (PSRS) and VidCruiter are both used throughout this selection process. You will be required to provide the name and contact information for two references; one reference must be a current/previous supervisor/manager.
For this selection process, we will communicate with you by email. You must provide a valid email address to which you wish to receive communication regarding this selection process. It is your responsibility to inform of any change of address, telephone number and / or email address. You must ensure to check/view your email accounts including spam, promotion or other folders regularly as there may be a deadline for responses. Candidates who respond past the deadline risk being removed from the selection process. Time-sensitive emails related to this selection process will be sent by email. description:

Benefits Program Specialist
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. You will be challenged, energized and motivated to excel in our environment.
Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.
With our defined-benefit pension plan, benefits, and high flexibility for work life balance - find out more about why we are annually ranked as one of Canada's top employers: Working Here - Bank of Canada
Find out more about the next steps in our Recruitment process .
About the role
We are seeking a Benefits Program Specialist to support the delivery, analysis, and continuous improvement of the Bank’s benefits program. In this role, you will contribute to projects and operational initiatives that strengthen program effectiveness, support informed decision-making, and enhance the employee experience.
Reporting to the Director of Compensation and Benefits, you will work as part of a collaborative Compensation and Benefits team and apply your benefits knowledge, analytical skills, and problem-solving abilities to support practical solutions and meaningful outcomes across the Bank.
What you will do
You will lead and contribute to projects and operational initiatives that enhance the effectiveness, sustainability, and employee experience of the Bank’s benefits program. You will apply your expertise, analytical skills, and project management discipline to identify opportunities for improvement, support informed decision-making, and help implement meaningful change for benefits and compensation programs.
In this role, you will:
- Use your knowledge of group benefit plan management to understand issues, explore options and help shape improvements.
- Help with planning, budgeting and the annual premium renewal by monitoring and analyzing costs, forecasts and emerging pressures.
- Turn information into insight by using data, reporting, technology, and AI to spot trends, improve processes, and simplify documentation.
- Partner with HR colleagues, benefits carriers and consultants to support service delivery .
- Bring people together to work through questions, align priorities, clarify next steps, and move benefits and compensation initiatives forward.
What you need to succeed
You are motivated by work that improves programs, processes, and the employee experience. You bring strong judgment, a practical mindset, and the ability to turn complex information and competing priorities into clear plans and simple messaging. You are also comfortable working with sensitive information and collaborating with others to move work forward.
You will thrive in this role if you can:
- consider the broader impact of changes to group benefits and insurance programs, ensuring they align with the Bank’s total compensation strategy and are coordinated with related HR teams, processes, and employee or retiree programs.
- make sense of information by turning data, trends, costs, and business questions into succinct insights that help people make good decisions.
- use good judgment to weigh options, understand risks, communicate clearly, and contribute to practical recommendations.
- enable projects to advance from idea to implementation by organizing priorities, managing timelines, and sharing progress.
- build strong relationships across teams by bringing people together to solve problems and align on next steps.
- look for better ways of working by using tools, technology, and practical improvements to strengthen processes, reporting, documentation, service delivery, and the employee experience.

- Experience with SAP SuccessFactors or a similar HRIS

- Project Management Professional (PMP) or related certification
Your education and experience
Your combined education and work experience demonstrate that you have the competencies required for the position and are effective at learning and applying new skills.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.
Language requirement The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. The position language requirement is Level 5 (Fully Functional). If a qualified candidate who meets the language requirement of the position is not found, a qualified candidate who does not meet the language requirement may be considered. Training may be provided to help reach the required level. Both bilingual and unilingual candidates are encouraged to apply.

Once the closing date has passed, it will no longer be available. The official title for this position is “Compensation and Benefits Specialist ”

The Bank offers work arrangements that provide employees with flexibility, enable high-performing teams, and support an excellent workplace culture. Most employees can telework from home for a portion of each month as part of the Bank’s hybrid work model, and they are expected on site at the Bank location a minimum of 12 days per month to help build connections between colleagues. You must live in Canada, and within reasonable commuting distance of the office.

We offer a competitive compensation and benefits package designed to meet your needs at every stage of your life and career. For more information on key benefits please visit A great deal to consider .

description:

Economist, Canadian Economic Analysis Department Rotation Program
Take a central role
The Bank of Canada has a vision to be a leading central bank—dynamic, engaged and trusted—committed to a better Canada. No other employer in the country offers you the unique opportunity to work at the very center of Canada’s economy, in an organization with significant impact on the economic and financial well-being of all Canadians. Building on the principles that have always guided us – excellence, integrity and respect – we strive to be forward-looking and innovative, to welcome people with diverse perspectives and talents, and to earn trust by living up to our commitments and by clearly explaining the intent of our policies and actions.

Interested in launching your career through a rotation? We are seeking an early-career economist to join the Rotation Program in the Canadian Economic Analysis (CEA) department. This structured program offers a broad experience across CEA while allowing you to contribute from the outset to high-impact analysis that informs monetary policy. Through the rotation, you will learn how economists at the Bank assess economic conditions in Canada, develop the economic outlook, and provide timely advice to support monetary policy decisions. Depending on your placement, you could assess and forecast key economic developments, contribute to staff economic projections or work with economists and researchers on rigorous, policy-relevant research that advances the understanding of the Canadian economy and contributes to the broader economics literature. You could also help develop the data, models, and analytical tools used across the department. You will turn complex economic information into clear briefings, research, and analytical products for senior management and Governing Council. After completing the rotation, you will be placed permanently in one division, where you can build on the expertise and relationships developed through the program.
What you will do
In this role, you will prepare and deliver insightful briefings to senior management and transform complex economic data into clear, actionable insights. Your analysis will help inform decisions that affect Canada’s economy. You will contribute to the Bank’s publications, including staff analytical papers and major reports like the Monetary Policy Report.
You will have opportunities to spend time on professional development. Whether it’s learning new software or exploring recent economic theories, continuous learning is a part of the role. As an economist in the Canadian Economic Analysis (CEA) department, you will conduct economic analysis and research that support the Bank’s assessment of the Canadian economy and inform monetary policy advice.
Examples of analytical work include:
- Designing new models and tools to monitor and forecast economic conditions
- Contributing to staff economic projections using large-scale macroeconomic models
- Analyzing information gathered through business and consumer surveys, regional outreach, and consultations to identify emerging economic trends and assess risks to the Canadian economic outlook
- Assessing the implications of major structural changes in the Canadian economy, such as demographic shifts, for growth, productivity, inflation, and the conduct of monetary policy
- Collaborating with economists and researchers on rigorous, longer-term research that advances the understanding of the Canadian economy and contributes to the broader economics literature
- E xamining fundamental questions in monetary economics, including the design of Canada’s monetary policy framework
What you need to succeed You have the ability to initiate and carry out rigorous research and analytical projects, and to use data and quantitative methods, including econometrics and time-series analysis, to develop evidence-based policy advice. You bring strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to evaluate alternatives and develop innovative solutions.
You demonstrate a high degree of intellectual curiosity and a commitment to continuous learning and self-development. You proactively identify emerging opportunities and translate them into forward-looking model development plans.
You collaborate effectively across teams and contribute to shared objectives. You are able to manage multiple projects, prioritize tasks, and ensure timely completion. You also have strong written and oral communication skills, with the ability to convey complex information clearly to varied audiences.
Nice-to-have
- Proficiency in programming with tools like Python, R, Stata, SQL, MATLAB, EViews, etc.
- Experience applying AI tools and methodologies to economic analysis, modelling, data processing, coding, and policy-relevant research
- Familiarity with Canadian data sources and concepts
Your education and experience The position requires a master’s degree in economics or finance.
Innovative Mindset
We value candidates who demonstrate adaptability, curiosity, and a willingness to learn new technologies, including AI and digital tools. We seek individuals who can think critically about data, question existing processes, and find ways to simplify our work while embracing change and new ways of doing things.

The Bank’s work environment is conducive to the use of both of Canada’s official languages - English and French. Although the position language requirement is English or French essential, we do encourage everyone to improve their second language proficiency for future career growth and to contribute towards fostering a bilingual environment.

title: Manager, Technology Sustainment
description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
The Canadian Air Transport Security Authority (CATSA) has 1 (one) exciting indeterminate opportunity within the Technology branch at the CATSA Headquarters.
This position represents an opportunity for career-driven individuals seeking a position within an organization that inspires growth and promotes excellence to make a difference and contribute to CATSA’s unique culture as it strives to excel in air transport security.
Why is CATSA a great fit for you?
CATSA is a world leader in aviation security, mandated to protect the public by delivering security screening operations at 89 designated airports across Canada. As a Crown corporation, CATSA is accountable to Parliament through the Minister of Transport.
We champion innovation and creativity and offer a welcoming and inclusive workplace where employees can be their true selves and take pride in being part of a mission that matters.
If you are a motivated professional seeking a position within a multifunctional and collaborative environment and you are looking for the next great adventure, CATSA is the place for you!
Summary of responsibilities:
The Manager, Technology Sustainment is responsible for providing strategic and technical leadership to ensure CATSA screening technologies remain supportable, reliable, compliant and future-ready throughout their lifecycle. The role leads technology governance, readiness, lifecycle management, modernization, reliability, spare parts strategy and data-driven continuous improvement. The Manager develops sustainment strategies, business cases and long-term plans to support operational readiness, technology performance and future technology needs. The Manager, Technology Sustainment, performs all other duties and responsibilities related to the position as required.
Key Tasks and Responsibilities:
- Managing all aspects of performance.
- Establish and maintain technology standards, governance frameworks, maintenance documentation, configuration controls and change management processes.
- Lead technology readiness, sustainment planning and lifecycle management activities, including roadmaps, obsolescence management, replacement planning and decommissioning strategies.
- Oversee maintenance optimization, failure analysis, predictive maintenance and technology performance improvement initiatives.
- Drive continuous improvement, KPI development and data-driven decision-making across the technology sustainment function.
What you need to succeed
To qualify for the position, you must have:
- Successful completion of a college diploma or university degree with specialization in project management, engineering, public administration, commerce or another specialty relevant to the duties of the position.
- A minimum of eight (8) years of experience in the lifecycle management of complex technology systems, including planning, deployment, sustainment, maintenance, operational support, and performance monitoring.
- Two to three years (2-3) years of management experience, leading a team.
- Experience developing recommendations and business cases that balance technical, operational, financial and lifecycle considerations.
- Experience leading technical assessments, operational readiness activities, performance improvement initiatives and data-driven decision-making for complex technology systems.
- Experience with budgeting, forecasting, procurement, contract management and stakeholder engagement.
- Experience planning and implementing technology deployments, upgrades, enhancements or disposal activities in an operational environment.
- Knowledge of technology lifecycle management, asset management, continuous improvement and governance principles.
This position is best suited to individuals with the following skills and abilities:
- Ability to provide strategic and technical leadership in support of organizational and operational objectives.
- Ability to lead, coach and develop high-performing teams in a collaborative and accountable environment.
- Strong analytical, problem-solving and decision-making skills (i.e., technical assessments, root cause analysis, business case development and risk-based decision-making).
- Ability to communicate effectively with technical and non-technical stakeholders, both orally and in writing.
- Ability to build relationships, influence decisions and collaborate effectively across multiple stakeholder groups (i.e., IT, OEMs, MSPs, Procurement and operational stakeholders).
- Ability to manage competing priorities and deliver results in a dynamic operational environment.
- Strong planning, organizational and resource management skills (i.e., technology readiness, lifecycle planning, budgeting and forecasting activities).
- Ability to use data, trends and performance information to support decision-making and continuous improvement (i.e., KPI development, reporting, performance analysis and planning activities).
- Strong stakeholder management and client-service orientation.
Valuable skills include:
- Experience working in an airport, transportation, or other regulated operational environment.
- Familiarity with security screening technologies or other complex technology systems.
- A Professional Engineer (P.Eng.) designation, PMP certification, or other related professional certification.
- Experience working with OEMs, maintenance service providers, suppliers, or contractors to support technology deployments, sustainment activities, or operational programs.
Specific work requirements :
- Ability to travel as required
- Language Profile: Bilingual (French and English), CBCC/CBCC
- Ability to obtain and maintain a Secret security clearance

Safeguarding Canada’s Financial Future: Through diligent regulation and supervision of FRFIs and FRPPs, we ensure that these entities operate soundly and securely. Our proactive approach to risk management and early intervention safeguards the interests of depositors, policyholders, pension plan members, and beneficiaries. We remain committed to fostering public confidence and supporting the competitive and resilient nature of Canada's financial landscape. Our Mandate: Our mandate is to ensure the stability and integrity of Canada's financial system. We achieve this by: Maintaining Financial Soundness: Ensuring that FRFIs and FRPPs remain in sound financial condition. Safeguarding Against Threats: Ensuring that FRFIs protect themselves against threats to their integrity and security, including foreign interference. Proactive Intervention: Acting swiftly when issues arise, requiring FRFIs and FRPPs to implement necessary corrective measures without delay. Risk Management: Continuously monitoring and evaluating risks, promoting sound risk management practices among FRFIs and FRPPs. Our Approach: In fulfilling our mandate, we adopt a balanced approach: For FRFIs: We protect the rights and interests of depositors, policyholders, and financial institution creditors. At the same time, we recognize the need for FRFIs to compete effectively and take reasonable risks. For FRPPs: We safeguard the rights and interests of pension plan members, former members, and entitled beneficiaries. Join Us: Be part of a system that ensures financial stability and security for all Canadians. Learn more about our work and how you can contribute to a stronger Canadian financial future. Follow Us: Twitter: @OSFICanada LinkedIn: Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions Canada

description:
Language requirements: Bilingual - imperative
Special posting considerations: The intent of this process is to staff two (2) positions: one (1) 24-month term appointment with the possibility of extension, acting, assignment, secondment, or exchange and one (1) indeterminate appointment. This process also aims to create a pool of partially and fully qualified candidates that may be used to staff similar term or indeterminate positions within both Agencies.
Candidates must clearly demonstrate in their cover letter how they meet the education and experience factors listed in the essential and asset qualifications. The cover letter should not exceed two (2) pages in English or two and half (2.5) pages in French* (8.5x11; 11 point font; normal margins). Please note that it is not sufficient to only state that the qualification is met; applicants must clearly indicate how they meet the merit criteria by providing concrete examples. Resumes will be used as a secondary source to validate the experience described in the cover letter. Failure to clearly demonstrate in your cover letter how you meet the screening criteria (education and experience) will result in the rejection of your application. Candidates will not be solicited for incomplete or possible missing information.
*The additional length of French cover letters recognizes anticipated differences in length to express similar content based on official language choice.
Who we are
This position falls within a directorate that provides common services to two funding agencies: the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC) and the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC).
At the Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council of Canada (SSHRC), we bring together the research community, as well as the public, private and not-for-profit sectors, in contributing knowledge, talent and expertise to build a better future for Canada and the world. SSHRC is seeking talented professionals passionate about Canadian research and the value it brings to society.
The Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council of Canada (NSERC) is Canada’s largest funder of science and engineering. A career at NSERC means supporting the visionaries, explorers and innovators who are searching for the scientific and technical breakthroughs that will advance knowledge, improve the lives of Canadians and transform the world for the better.
Visit our career page at SSHRC or NSERC to learn more about why you should join our agency.
What you will do
As an Evaluation Manager, your responsibilities will include:
Leadership and direction in the delivery of performance measurement, evaluation and review services including the provision of strategic and authoritative advice to senior management of the Natural Sciences and Engineering Research Council (NSERC)‘s, Social Sciences and Humanities Research Council (SSHRC)’s and Inter-Agency programs and other external stakeholders to optimize the effective and sound evaluation, assessment, and analysis of the performance of NSERC’s, SSHRC’s and Inter-Agency programs and associated policies.
What you need to succeed
Education
- Master’s degree from a recognized university with a specialisation in evaluation, economics, sociology, statistics, or social sciences research methods, OR an acceptable combination of education, training, and relevant work experience with a specialization in one of these fields. A graduate diploma in program evaluation would also be acceptable.
- Foreign Credential Validation against Canadian Standards
Experience
- Extensive 1 experience conducting evaluations of programs, including those involving multiple organizations, consistent with the Federal Government’s policies related to evaluation.
- Extensive 1 experience applying a range of evaluation methods, including both qualitative and quantitative techniques.
- Experience supervising or managing human resources.
- Extensive 1 experience analyzing data, synthesizing evaluation findings and presenting results to senior management.
- Experience evaluating research or research related activities, and/or grants and contribution programs would be an asset .
1 Extensive is equivalent to five (5) or more years of experience.
Knowledge
- Knowledge of program evaluation theory and practices, including federal government performance measurement and evaluation policies/standards.
- Knowledge of evaluation methods and approaches, including qualitative and quantitative analysis techniques.
- Knowledge of project management principles.
- Knowledge of the post-secondary research funding environment, the research process and the transfer of research results to the user sector would be an asset .
Competencies
- Client service and delivery oriented.
- Analytical thinking (analysis and problem-solving).
- Effective oral and written communication.
- Demonstrate initiative and flexibility, and act with confidence.
Key Leadership Competencies
- Create Vision and Strategy.
- Mobilize People.
- Uphold integrity and respect.
- Collaboration with Partners and Stakeholders.
- Promote Innovation and Guide Change.
- Achieve Results.
Equity, diversity and inclusion
We are committed to inclusive and barrier-free recruitment to create a workforce that reflects the Canadians we serve. We promote employment equity and encourage you to indicate if you belong to one of the designated groups when you apply.
We welcome all candidates, and encourage applications from women, Indigenous Peoples (First Nations, Métis and Inuit), veterans, persons with disabilities, Black and other racialized persons, persons of ethnic origins, diverse religions, abilities, sexual orientations, gender identities and expressions, and members of the 2SLGBTQIA+ community.
Accommodation
Let our team know if you require accommodation or support during the recruitment process by contacting us at recruiting@nserc-crsng.gc.ca .
If you require additional information on the position, please contact us at recruiting@nserc-crsng.gc.ca .

About CMHC
The work you do and the work we do together matters. We come to work every day with a common purpose: to contribute to a well-functioning housing system.
At CMHC, we hold ourselves accountable for our results and support our colleagues in their achievements. We thrive on collaboration, connecting across CMHC and involving the right people to get our work done. Our leadership style is guided by trust , where our leaders favour an adaptive approach based on the needs of their teams.
Join us and be part of a team that's committed to making a real difference and be part of something meaningful.
Our commitment to diversity, equity, and inclusion
We're committed to advancing employment equity and fostering an inclusive workplace. To reflect the diversity of Canada’s population, we encourage applications from women, Indigenous Peoples, persons with disabilities, 2SLGBTQI+ individuals, veterans, and racialized peoples. We also welcome applications from all individuals eligible to work in Canada.
We are also committed to advancing reconciliation with Indigenous Peoples and supporting the meaningful inclusion of First Nations, Inuit, and Métis voices and priorities. While this position is hybrid requiring some in-office presence, a work from home arrangement may be considered for First Nations candidates on reserve or Indigenous candidates that reside further than 125KM from a CMHC office.

What’s in it for you
We’ve got the purpose, the people and the perks you need for a fulfilling career. Here’s the comprehensive and generous benefits you get when you’re a permanent employee:
- Annual Paid vacation.
- Annual individual performance incentive.
- Defined benefit pension plan.
- Comprehensive group insurance plan to support your well-being from day one.

About the role
Join the Multi Unit Risk Management, Strategy & Products team under the direction of Steve Mckinnon, in the Specialist, Operational Policy Analysis position, where our partners view CMHC as the catalyst for solving housing affordability challenges. You will provide research, conceptualization and development of information, analysis and recommendations; lead or act as a member of a multi-disciplinary team; lead the conceptualization, development and implementation of new and/or existing policies, products, services and/or systems; and continually ensure that client needs are met throughout the process.
What you’ll do:
- Obtain input from internal and external stakeholders and clients on issues and opportunities related to policies, products, services and/or systems.
- Lead or contribute to the development of strategies, policies, work plans and risk management for the sector and for other sectors within CMHC, as appropriate.

Work environment
Help shape the future of Canada, one conversation at a time!
Every year, Statistics Canada connects with millions of Canadians to collect information that helps inform decisions on issues that matter, including health, employment, housing, business, and the economy.
As a Data Collection Clerk, you will be on the front lines of data collection, engaging directly with Canadians and businesses in your community. About the position
Duties
Under the general direction of the Facilities Manager, the Assistant Facilities Manager:
• Assists in the planning, coordination, and delivery of facilities management programs and services for buildings and infrastructure.
• Monitors the operation and condition of building systems including mechanical, electrical, plumbing, HVAC, and life-safety systems.
• Conducts facility inspections and identifies maintenance, repair, operational, and safety requirements.
• Coordinates and monitors the work of contractors, consultants, and service providers engaged in maintenance, repair, and construction activities.
• Assists in the development, implementation, and monitoring of preventative maintenance and asset management programs.
• Participates in the planning, coordination, and administration of facilities-related projects from initiation through completion.
• Supports procurement activities including development of statements of work, technical requirements, cost estimates, and contract administration.
• Ensures activities are conducted in accordance with applicable legislation, codes, standards, departmental policies, and occupational health and safety requirements.
• Responds to operational issues, emergencies, and service disruptions to support the continuity of facility operations.
Work environment
The Assistant Facilities Manager works in a dynamic environment supporting the operation, maintenance, and improvement of federal facilities and infrastructure. The position involves a combination of office and field work, including inspections of buildings, mechanical and electrical systems, construction sites, and research facilities. The incumbent works closely with tradespeople, contractors, project teams, scientists, and stakeholders to support facility operations, maintenance programs, and capital projects. Occasional travel within the local area, on-call responsibilities, and response to operational emergencies may be required.

- A deep expertise in one or more D365 platforms, including Customer Engagement (Sales, Customer Service, Marketing), Finance & Operations, and Customer Insights.
- A strong knowledge of the Microsoft Power Platform, including Power Apps, Power Automate, and Dataverse.
- A proven experience designing and implementing enterprise integration architectures and patterns.
- A strong proficiency with REST and SOAP APIs and enterprise integration technologies.
- An experience with Azure Integration Services, Azure Logic Apps, Service Bus, and event-driven architectures.
- An expertise in data integration, synchronization, and troubleshooting distributed systems and complex production environments.
- A solid understanding of security, authentication, authorization, enterprise architecture principles, and experience working in Agile and DevOps environments.

- Microsoft Dynamics 365 certifications.
- Azure Architect or Azure Integration certifications.
- Experience with enterprise middleware platforms.
- Experience supporting highly integrated and mission-critical business platforms.
- Knowledge of data architecture, analytics, and reporting solutions.

employer: Administrative Tribunals Support Service of Canada
